Here is a concise, integrated 12-week program for your client (36, recreational lifter, post‑meniscal repair with surgeon clearance for low‑impact strength). It combines strength, conditioning (cardio), peak weeks, recovery, mobility, and nutrition to support strength gains and a safe return to skiing. The plan preserves knee-friendly ROM, emphasizes glute/hamstring balance, hip and ankle stability, core control, upper body strength for skiing technique, and ski-transfer capacity.

Overall structure
- Frequency: 4 training days per week (Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B), with 2 knee-friendly cardio sessions integrated (these can be scheduled on off days or after upper-body days as needed).
- Phases:
  - Weeks 1–3: Foundation, technique, knee-tolerant development, establish movement quality.
  - Weeks 4–8: Progressive overload with increased volume (volume block) and intensified cardio while maintaining knee safety.
  - Weeks 9–12: Peak strength and ski-readiness with a planned taper and ski-transfer emphasis, culminating in Week 12 testing and readiness checks.
- Progression: conservative load increases on main lifts (2.5–5% weekly where tolerated), added sets/accessory volume weeks 4–8, and a structured peak in weeks 11–12 with reduced total volume but high-quality reps.
- Safety: no jumping, no deep-knee flexion under load, no deep knee flexion during loaded movements, auto-regulation for any knee discomfort, ROM kept within knee-tolerant ranges, tempo 2–3 seconds eccentric, 1 second pause, 1–2 seconds concentric.

Weekly template (example)
- Day A: Upper body push/pull + core
- Day B: Lower body hinge/safe quad emphasis + glute/hamstring focus
- Day C: Upper body push/pull (different angles) + core
- Day D: Lower body stability, mobility, ski-transfer relevant work
- Cardio: 2 knee-friendly sessions per week (options: incline treadmill intervals, bike intervals, ski-sim circuit). Keep total cardio volume moderate and progressive.

12-week week-by-week plan (highlights with sample structure)

Weeks 1–3: Foundation and technique
- Goals: establish quality movement, activate glutes/hamstrings, retrain knee mechanics, begin gradual strength gains.
- Sample structure (4 days):
  - Day A (Upper): Supersets — incline DB press 3×8–10, seated row 3×8–10; DB shoulder press 3×10; lat pulldown 3×10; Pallof press 3×12 per side; optional face pulls.
  - Day B (Lower): Romanian deadlift 3×8–10; goblet squat to shallow depth 3×8–10; glute bridge 3×12; Nordic hamstring or hamstring curl 3×8–10; step-ups to a low platform 3×8 per leg; calves 3×12; core 3×8 per side.
  - Day C (Upper): Flat DB press 3×8–10; cable row 3×8–10; lateral raises 3×12; face pulls 3×12; core circuit.
  - Day D (Lower): Split squats to shallow depth 3×8 per leg; hip thrust 3×8–10; clamshells 3×12; single-leg balance 3×30s per leg; mobility work.
- Cardio: 1–2 low-intensity sessions, 20–30 minutes total; incline/low-impact emphasis.
- Progression: +5–10% load where tolerance allows; maintain knee-friendly ROM; focus on tempo (2–3 sec eccentric).

Weeks 4–5: Volume ramp with knee-friendly load
- Increase total sets per lift on main moves; add 1–2 accessory moves per lower day.
- Example Day A: incline press 4×8–10; row 4×8–10; dumbbell shoulder press 3×10–12; lat pulldown 3×10–12; Pallof press 3×12; optional band pull-aparts.
- Day B: RDL 4×6–8; goblet squat to shallow depth 4×8–10; hip thrust 4×12; hamstring curl 3×8–10; step-ups 3–4×8 per leg; calves 4×12; core circuit.
- Day C: flat DB press 4×8–10; row 4×8–10; lateral raises 3×12; face pulls 3×12; core anti-rotation 3×10 per side.
- Day D: front-foot elevated split squats 3×8 per leg; hip thrust 4×8–10; glute bridge tempo 3×12; single-leg balance 3×40s; mobility.
- Cardio: 2 sessions with modestly higher volume or intervals (knee-friendly).

Weeks 6–7: Volume intensification
- Push main lifts to 4×8–10 or 4×6–8 with strong tolerable loads; add minor intensifications in accessory work.
- Day A: incline press 4×8; row 4×8; overhead press 4×6–8; lat pulldown 3×8–10; pallof press.
- Day B: RDL 4×6–8; goblet squat shallow 4×8–10; hip thrust 4×10–12; hamstring curl 3×8–10; step-ups 4×8 per leg; calves 4×12.
- Day C: DB/BB press 4×8–10; row 4×8; lateral raises 3×12; face pulls 3×12; core.
- Day D: split squats 3×8; hip thrust 4×8–10; glute bridge tempo 3×12; single-leg balance 3×40s; mobility.
- Cardio: 2 sessions with slight intensity increase; rotate modalities for engagement.

Weeks 8: Peak volume week (pre-peak)
- Main lifts at higher total sets; aim for 4–5×5 or 4×6 depending on tolerance.
- Accessory density increased lightly; maintain knee-friendly ROM.
- Cardio: 2–3 sessions but with slightly higher total volume (steady-state or intervals) as tolerated.

Weeks 9–10: Build toward peak
- Maintain 4 days; reduce overall fatigue slightly to prepare for peak, but keep high-quality reps.
- Day A/B/C/D maintain strong lifting pattern with 4–6 reps on main lifts when possible, but capped to protect the knee.
- Cardio: 2 sessions; keep volume moderate to support recovery.

Weeks 11–12: Peak weeks (strength expression and ski-readiness)
- Week 11: Heavy-but-controlled week
  - Day A Upper: 4×4–5 at 86–92% or equivalent RPE 8–9; accessories reduced.
  - Day B Lower: 3–4×4–6 hinge/quad-friendly patterns; tempo 2–3 sec eccentric.
  - Day C Upper: 4×4–6 incline/bench; accessories limited.
  - Day D Lower: 2–3×4–6 shallow split squats or goblet squats; hip thrust 3–4×6–8; core.
  - Cardio: 1–2 light sessions for recovery.
- Week 12: Peak and testing
  - Day A Upper: 2–3×3–4 at 85–90%; minimal accessories.
  - Day B Lower: 2–3×3–5 with focus on technique; avoid deep knee flexion under load.
  - Day C Upper: 2–3×3–4; ramped sets, no grinder reps.
  - Day D Lower: ski-transfer activation; light goblet squats to shallow ROM; unilateral glute work.
  - Testing: 1–2 non-fatiguing performance checks (e.g., 3–5 rep max re-test on 1–2 main lifts, ski-transfer balance tests, edge control drills).

Nutrition and cardio integration (throughout)
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day (target around 1.8 g/kg as baseline).
- Calories: maintain maintenance; on days with higher volume or cardio, small carb boosts around training sessions.
- Carbs: adjust to support training load; higher around heavy or cardio days; keep fats moderate to meet total calories.
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L/day baseline; more on cardio days; consider electrolytes for longer sessions.
- Meal timing: pre-workout 20–40 g carbs + 15–25 g protein; post-workout 25–40 g protein + 60–80 g carbs.

Recovery, mobility, and ski-readiness
- Daily mobility: 5–12 minutes focusing on hips, knees (gentle ROM), ankles, thoracic spine.
- Dedicated mobility sessions: 2× per week (15–20 minutes) focusing on hip/knee ROM, ankle mobility, and thoracic mobility.
- Sleep: 7–9 hours nightly; wind-down routine to improve sleep quality.
- Recovery modalities: foam rolling, light percussion, contrast baths as available.
- Knee care: monitor swelling/pain; back off ROM or load if pain arises. Prioritize glute/hammstring control to unload the knee.
- Ski-transfer readiness: integrate balance/edge drills, single-leg stability, and hip external rotation work in warm-ups and cooldowns.

Delivery format options
- Full plan can be delivered as a detailed week-by-week calendar with exact exercises, each day’s sets/reps/tempo, and progression targets.
- I can provide a printable 2-page recovery/mobility cheat sheet for daily use.
- A simple tracking sheet can be supplied to monitor weekly knee comfort, perceived exertion, weights, and cardio volume.

Next steps (optional)
- I can tailor the plan to his exact numbers (current 1RM estimates or conservative targets, body weight, height, equipment access).
- I can generate a fully detailed 12-week schedule with day-by-day exercise order, precise rep ranges, tempo, rest intervals, and progression matrix.
- I can create a weekly nutrition calendar with exact macro targets for weeks 1–12, plus a 7-day rotating meal plan and grocery list, and a cardio calendar aligned to rehab days.
